title: Cells architecture
caveat: Capabilities vary by model, and whole-cell integration is ongoing. No single run uses every part drawn here.

statuses.label: Qualified or judged
statuses.description: Numerically qualified (a registered protocol passed) or judged (used in a registered experiment), in its declared scope.

statuses.label: Implemented and guarded
statuses.description: On main with its tests and guards: the plan's 'implemented' and 'guarded' levels. Not yet qualified by a registered protocol.

statuses.label: Established
statuses.description: Built earlier and in routine use: older model families and shared infrastructure. Scope and evidence are in each guide.

statuses.label: Designed
statuses.description: A design or protocol is written or accepted; the code is not on main.

statuses.label: Planned
statuses.description: Named in the plan or roadmap; not started.

statuses.label: Failed qualification
statuses.description: Built, then failed its registered qualification. Kept as evidence and not relied on.

statuses.label: External reference
statuses.description: Outside the engine: a reference simulator or data set, run out of process and compared through saved outputs.

representations.label: Simulated
representations.description: The engine evolves this state step by step, with material, charge and energy accounted for.

representations.label: Modelled in aggregate
representations.description: Represented as a population, count or rate law, not as individual molecules. Shapes drawn for it are illustrations.

representations.label: Prescribed
representations.description: Happens on a schedule the experiment sets; the cell does not decide it.

representations.label: Illustration only
representations.description: Drawn for orientation. Nothing in the engine stands behind it yet.

model_groups.label: Composite tissue model
model_groups.description: resolved_pump_composite@1: the pump tissue model's own step plus declared operators. These parts run together in one model today. Its inner tissue model is being rebuilt in place as one modular model; that work is not on main.

model_groups.label: Earlier tissue families
model_groups.description: The older resolved-tissue families, one module per feature combination. Calcium, fuel, mitochondria, regulation and repair run together here. Their physics moves into the composite model in stages, as uses need it (D167).

model_groups.label: Separate engines
model_groups.description: Models that run on their own: protein-cage assembly, vertex mechanics and the regulatory circuits.

layers.label: Execution
layers.description: How a definition becomes a checked, restartable run.

layers.label: Numerics
layers.description: Time stepping, field solves and long-time methods.

layers.label: Shared state
layers.description: The entities that own physical state. Mechanisms that affect the same thing change the same state.

layers.label: Physical laws
layers.description: Transport, kinetics, chemistry, geometry and mechanics, one law per module.

layers.label: Models
layers.description: Versioned model families built from the laws.

layers.label: Operators
layers.description: Laws declared as operators of the composite tissue model.

layers.label: Experiments
layers.description: Clients of the engine: parity checks, morphogenesis, division and heredity.

layers.label: References and validation
layers.description: Outside the engine: reference simulators run out of process, independent reference solutions and the test gate.

layers.label: Plan gates
layers.description: The current plan's gates, in order, from docs/CURRENT_PLAN.md.

components.label: CPU, float64
components.plain: Every model runs on ordinary processors in double precision. These runs are the reference that GPU runs are checked against.

components.label: NVIDIA L4 GPU
components.plain: One GPU runs many independent worlds at once. All 12 BETSE parity protocols also pass on it, under registered GPU variants. Under a deterministic setting, repeated runs of the 825-node tissue are identical bit for bit; the rework's GPU checks use it as a declared mode (D181).

components.label: Ensemble workers
components.plain: Workers take batches of independent simulations from a shared queue, one persistent process per GPU.

components.label: JUPITER GH200
components.plain: A supercomputer allocation of 10,000 GPU-hours. The recipe and runbook are ready; nothing has run there, and its speed is unmeasured.

components.label: One world across GPUs
components.plain: Splitting one large interacting tissue across several devices. No code does this; it is added only if single-device measurements justify it.

components.label: Command line
components.plain: The command that runs a model from a configuration file and writes its results and checkpoints.

components.label: Definitions
components.plain: Each run is declared as data: the model, the experiment and how to execute it. Definitions are checked before anything runs.

components.label: Model registry
components.plain: Finds the model code for a definition. Today it is an ordered chain of type checks.

components.label: Declarative registry
components.plain: One table saying how each model takes part in parsing, saving, controls, execution and checkpoints.

components.label: External modules
components.plain: Packages maintained outside Cells could add laws and mechanisms that meet the same checks, accounting and execution contracts as the engine's own. Cells stays under the MIT licence, aiming at broad use (the user's direction, D180, 15 November 2026). Each part would be registered explicitly for one model build, then checked, assembled, compiled and run; registering a module that a model does not use changes nothing. The design is proposed, not yet adopted. The modular rework leaves four openings for it. Its first stage, one law from a separately installed package, starts after the rework lands, and five decisions in it are the user's. Today the engine's registries are closed tables inside Cells. Not on main.

components.label: State and resources
components.plain: State is held as explicit arrays with fixed capacities and masks; memory needs are estimated before a run starts.

components.label: Schedules
components.plain: Timed changes an experiment makes, such as blocking a pump or a junction, applied at exact times.

components.label: Phase markers
components.plain: Records that mark where each phase of a run started, ended or failed. Completion records came first; start and failure records landed on 15 November 2026 for every run path.

components.label: Single-world runner
components.plain: Runs one world step by step with every check, in bounded windows. A reference path.

components.label: Guarded batch
components.plain: Runs many independent worlds, each on its own clock, with rows checked on the host.

components.label: Batch windows
components.plain: Runs cohorts of worlds in bounded rounds, with complete cohort checkpoints.

components.label: Vector windows
components.plain: Advances many worlds as one vectorised batch with the checks on the device. The candidate for the one production path.

components.label: One production path
components.plain: Naming one execution path for production and declaring the others as reference paths, with shared admission and checkpoint checks.

components.label: Compile policy
components.plain: A rule for what is compiled into a program and what is passed in, with a budget for compile time and memory.

components.label: Run-view output
components.plain: Every run will save what a viewer needs to replay it: geometry, identities, record metadata, events and how each layer is represented. The requirement is recorded (D154), and its design note is proposed (15 November 2026). Its code joins the modular rework: a writer is built on a branch of its own, with a worked example on a development run. It merges after the rework lands, followed by the viewer's requests and a first living-cell loop (FR-11). Not on main.

components.label: Living-cell loops (FR-11)
components.plain: Short replay packages that show each species' cell alive, in a loop, whenever no research run is being explored (the user's request, 15 November 2026). It is output, not new physics: each package is a short run of laws the engine has, at a low level of detail, and is labelled an illustration, never a result. The user chose periodic loops, with one period of a periodic drive played and its seam checked; a paced heart cell for human; and, for the minimal cells, their cycle of growth and division, as an illustration. Logged; it comes after the run-view writer, with a planarian loop first.

components.label: GPU-native execution
components.plain: What the rebuilt core must show on a GPU. A mechanism that is not declared is absent from the compiled program. A change of parameters alone reuses the compiled program. Stepping, step checks and refusals stay on the device, with no Python per cell and no CPU solver in the production loop. Compile time, memory and end-to-end time are measured on representative worlds. Today this holds in the vector-window path only, where steps and their checks run inside one compiled program; elsewhere these are targets, and an audit of the exceptions is pending. The audit's tests land with the rework. In development on the integration branch since 15 November 2026; not on main.

components.label: Packed GPU execution
components.plain: Many worlds of one structure packed into one batch on the GPU, to keep it busy. On the L4, one world of the 825-node tissue keeps about a quarter of the GPU's processors active; 128 worlds or more keep about 90% active. The same planner would serve the rework's GPU checks and production ensembles. Its design was proposed on 15 November 2026, at the user's request, and a planner is built on a branch of its own. In a development run on the L4 on 16 November 2026, packed repeats were identical bit for bit, but packing alone moved some small flux and ledger values by up to 1.6e-8 relative, more than the criterion set for it; that needs a basis before its qualification. Not on main.

components.label: Organism definitions
components.plain: A place for what is specific to one organism: its strain, conditions, parameter values and the evidence behind them, kept apart from the engine's mechanisms. The engine has none today: worlds are built by code and fixtures, and no organism is defined. The architecture document sets it as a target that lands with the first milestone that needs it, and the minimal-cell track's note proposes one. A new organism should then add engine physics only for a mechanism the engine lacks.

components.label: Device placement
components.plain: Says explicitly whether work runs on a CPU or a GPU.

components.label: Checkpoints and files
components.plain: Saves complete checkpoints, so a run can restart exactly or branch into alternative futures.

components.label: Checkpoint continuity
components.plain: Lets a checkpoint written by one version of the code resume under another, but only through a recorded admission. Refusal stays the default. In place for CPU vector windows, and on the GPU for its first case, whose extension landed on 14 November 2026.

components.label: Observers
components.plain: Read-only measurements taken from a run. Observing never changes the dynamics.

components.label: Tissue preparation
components.plain: Prepares a tissue before an experiment and hands its full state to the next phase, with no silent re-equilibration.

components.label: Cell removal
components.plain: Cuts cells out of a tissue and continues the run, keeping the surviving material and its history.

components.label: Other core modules
components.plain: Core modules not grouped elsewhere on this map.

components.label: Checked RK4
components.plain: A fixed-step integrator that checks every trial state and refuses a failed step; it never repairs one.

components.label: IMEX step
components.plain: The tissue models' time step, treating the fast electrical part implicitly. It refactorises a dense matrix every step, which limits tissue size.

components.label: Field solvers
components.plain: Solve for the voltages that keep charge consistent across membranes and the space between cells. Limited to 2,048 electrical nodes today.

components.label: Field-solver interface
components.plain: An interface that keeps the field law and its checks while allowing sparse or matrix-free solvers. Designed; its code waits for the GH200 measurements.

components.label: Transport kernels
components.plain: Shared array kernels for moving ions across membranes and junctions.

components.label: Gate updates
components.plain: Exact exponential updates for channel gates.

components.label: Water step
components.plain: The numerical step for water flow and volume change.

components.label: Membrane redistribution
components.plain: Moves channels and pumps along the membrane while conserving their number.

components.label: Projective stepping
components.plain: A long-time mode that takes bursts of fine steps and then jumps ahead. It failed its qualification on the absolute error caps.

components.label: Fixed points
components.plain: Finds a tissue's resting states and follows them as parameters change. Passed all 16 criteria of its protocol.

components.label: Long-time methods
components.plain: Multirate or quasi-steady stepping for hours to months of biology. A verdict on them is a deliverable of the compute-limits gate; its acceptance now includes an intervention applied during the slow phase (feature request FR-8, D164).

components.label: State roles and step time
components.plain: Each field will declare what kind of state it is: something that evolves continuously, something set by an algebraic rule, an accumulated history, or a discrete event. Counters will say whether they count numerical steps or physical events. A numerical plan will carry its interval and the next event that must not be stepped over, so that a future long step respects doses, regulatory changes and timed events. These are interfaces only: the rework specifies and reserves them, and they are built with their first user, the long-duration mode (feature request FR-8). Fixed-step limits stay until then. Not on main.

components.label: Mechanical analysis
components.plain: Finds mechanical equilibria of a cell sheet and infers junction tensions from its shape. Qualified with the vertex model.

components.label: Other numerics
components.plain: Numerics and analysis modules not grouped elsewhere on this map.

components.label: Membrane transport
components.plain: Ions cross membranes driven by concentration and voltage, with each transfer counted once.

components.label: Channel catalogue
components.plain: 56 sodium, potassium, HCN, calcium and leak channel laws. The heredity channels NaV1.2 and Kir2.1 pass BETSE parity.

components.label: Pumps
components.plain: The sodium–potassium pump and the calcium pumps, which spend ATP to move ions uphill.

components.label: Gap junctions
components.plain: Gated channels between neighbouring cells, and the law by which a new cell forms its junctions over time.

components.label: Cotransport
components.plain: Carriers that move two kinds of ion together, including the potassium–anion symport cells use to regulate volume.

components.label: Reactions
components.plain: Chemical reactions inside compartments, with mass and energy accounted for.

components.label: Calcium and IP3
components.plain: Calcium release from the ER store, IP3 signalling and calcium entry at the membrane.

components.label: Fuel and mitochondria
components.plain: Finite pools of ATP that pumps draw on, and passive ion exchange with mitochondria. Respiration is not modelled.

components.label: Network regulation
components.plain: Rules that let ion levels and fuel regulate pumps, channels and junctions.

sources.where: Live network regulation of pumps, channels and junctions

components.label: Injury and resealing
components.plain: A membrane injury that leaks ions and reseals on a set schedule.

components.label: Physiological noise
components.plain: Random variation with explicit, repeatable random streams.

components.label: Tissue geometry
components.plain: Builds cells as polygons with explicit volumes, areas and neighbours.

components.label: Extracellular grid
components.plain: A grid for ions and currents in the space around cells.

components.label: Charged-surface backend
components.plain: Array kernels for charge-consistent membrane surfaces.

components.label: Vertex mechanics
components.plain: The forces in a sheet of cells, from edge tension and area elasticity. Topology is fixed: cells cannot yet swap neighbours.

components.label: Topology changes
components.plain: Cells swapping neighbours, leaving the sheet and dividing within it, with ions, charge and energy conserved.

components.label: Coupling out of the inventory
components.plain: The rule by which a species amount in the inventory sets how available a junction or a channel population is, so chemistry can change electrical behaviour. It is in the engine since 14 November 2026: the Hill factors, the operator that applies them to junctions and to channels, and a slower two-state regulatory state. The operator was numerically qualified on 15 November 2026, on CPU and within its stated scope. It also answers feature request FR-6, species-driven control factors.

components.label: Excitable tissue
components.plain: General physics for tissue that carries a travelling electrical wave, to be qualified against cable theory. The design note is accepted narrowly (D170, 14 November 2026), for its first two milestones on the tissue model as it stands. The probe registered for the acceptance failed its first criterion, so the acceptance rests on a second probe, post hoc but written before its runs. The first milestone's development work landed on 15 November 2026 as validation code only, with a proposed qualification protocol; nothing is judged yet, and the junction floor stays provisional. Its new channel and junction laws enter after the modular rework, as declared pieces. No new engine code yet.

components.label: Gene regulation in tissue
components.plain: Gene networks that set how much of each protein is made, coupled to the tissue's physiology.

components.label: Golgi and trafficking
components.plain: The pathway that carries new proteins from the ER through the Golgi to the membrane or out of the cell. Planned, not started.

components.label: Laws as declared pieces
components.plain: Today the tissue model's own channel laws are a closed table: they are computed for every channel population and selected afterwards, even in a world that has no channels. In the rework each channel law, junction law, pump family, fuel kind and solver is a piece of its own, chosen when a world's program is built, so a mechanism that is not declared is absent from the program. A probe found that separating the laws moves no result: in seven worlds every value at every step stayed the same bit for bit, with smaller programs. The operators already declare what they read, change and book, through the operator contract. Built on the integration branch by 15 November 2026, where the saved worlds give the same results bit for bit; not on main.

components.label: One identity per species
components.plain: Each kind of molecule gets one identity and one conserved total, declared once where a world is defined, however many arrays hold it: free and bound molecules of one kind are one species. New laws then need no checks against each other's species lists, which operators make pair by pair today. Sums over species follow one declared order everywhere, so that raising the limit on the number of species later needs only a check on one test world and a cost measurement. The order was settled on 16 November 2026 (D182): every such sum adds the species one at a time, in their declared order. Measured on the L4, it costs no measurable time at 16 species, and its sums come out bit for bit the same on the GPU and the CPU. It moves only ledgers and diagnostics, at rounding: in all 113 saved worlds every physical quantity stayed the same bit for bit. It is the round's last change, made alone. The species registry and this order are built on the integration branch; not on main.

components.label: Fuel as shared species
components.plain: Decided on 15 November 2026 (D176): ATP, ADP and phosphate become ordinary species of the shared inventory. Reactions make and spend them, pumps draw from the same amounts, and the standard chemical potential of each is declared in one place. In the design, finite fuel is a transporter's default, and fuel held constant is the special case: a held row of that inventory, not a parameter of a pump. The first case is small: one regeneration reaction and one pump share a finite amount of fuel, and show depletion, a slower pump and recovery. Its independent reference landed on main on 15 November 2026: with regeneration stopped for 200 s, ATP falls almost to nothing and the pump to about 0.2% of its rate; two seconds after regeneration resumes the pump is back within 1%, and every account closes. The engine's own case is checked against it after the rework lands. Two boundaries are still open: how this meets explicit proton chemistry, and that work booked by a reaction is not fuel. Today finite fuel exists only in the earlier tissue families, and the tissue model holds its fuel constant. Designed; not on main.

components.label: Passive permeation law
components.plain: A law for molecules that cross a membrane on their own, down their gradient. In a closed test with two compartments it must conserve material, stop when both sides are at equal chemical potential, reverse with the driving force, and turn the free energy lost into heat with no work from outside. The engine's present operator for secretion and uptake is a driven route that books work, so it does not count as passive. This is the one law added in the rework round, to show that adding a law changes nothing for worlds that do not use it; its core computation already exists in the tissue model's own membrane transport. The minimal-cell track's vesicle tests are its first user. Its independent reference landed on main on 15 November 2026, written by a separate agent that read no engine code: in it, flow and heat are exactly zero at equal concentrations, the flow reverses exactly, and heat never decreases. The law is built on the integration branch, with the heat it releases booked exactly; not on main.

components.label: Levels of detail
components.plain: A mechanism can be represented in more or less detail, chosen for each mechanism and each question: no single detail level holds for a whole world. Two representations of one mechanism show the same quantities at their physical interface, each closes its own ledgers, and the difference between them belongs to a declared error budget. A reduced one must remove real work, not hide the detailed one behind a switch. Set in the architecture document on 15 November 2026 (D175) as a target. Today the representation chosen is recorded with every run, and nothing yet stops two representations of one pathway from running together. Its fields are reserved in the modular rework's law design, and its first use comes after the first fuel case. Not on main.

components.label: First bounded models
components.plain: The first small models: one cell, a pair, a regulatory circuit and small graphs of cells. Each was accepted in its own bounded scope.

components.label: Finite and spatial exterior
components.plain: Models where the fluid outside cells is a finite, spatial inventory with its own ions and fields.

components.label: Calcium and chemistry
components.plain: Models of calcium stores, IP3 signalling and compartment chemistry, tested on synthetic cases.

components.label: Pump tissue @1–@3

components.label: Water and volume
components.plain: The pump tissue with osmotic water, changing cell volume and volume regulation. Now a thin composition of operators.

components.label: Cell replacement
components.plain: The pump tissue with scheduled replacement of cells. Now a thin composition of operators.

components.label: Composite tissue model
components.plain: The newer design: the pump tissue's own step plus declared operators, so new combinations are definitions and not new model modules. Numerically qualified on CPU through its frozen-model guards and judged in E07-v1. On the L4 GPU it agrees within the registered tolerance (W1, W2, and Q1 to Q6 of G2-Q1 pass); the one criterion that asks for bitwise equality failed on the judged run, from the GPU's own nondeterminism. Judged alone under a deterministic GPU setting on 16 November 2026, it passed, in that setting only.

components.label: Modular inner model
components.plain: The tissue model is being rebuilt in place as one modular model: each channel law, junction law, pump family, fuel kind and solver becomes a separate declared piece, and a world compiles only the pieces it declares. No second inner model is kept beside it, and the model keeps its name (the user's decision, D172; D176). The work is in implementation since 15 November 2026, as one round on an integration branch, and is not on main. It is accepted by results, not by identical programs: existing worlds must give the same results, and every affected registered protocol is run again. The user held one re-run, E07-v1's: its worlds are covered by the results comparison instead (D181). On 16 November 2026 the round's candidate passed the first steps of its final checks. All 113 saved worlds gave the same results: bit for bit before the round's last change, the order of sums over species (D182), and within its declared tolerance after it, with every physical quantity still bit for bit. Every registered small protocol was run again and passed. Part of its GPU checks and the third tier of tests stopped for a planned restart before any verdict was written, and resume after it. The parts it delivers are its outline: each says what holds today, what lands in the round and what is only reserved there.

components.label: Resolved tissue families
components.plain: The older design: one module for each combination of calcium, fuel, water, repair, profiles and interventions. Kept frozen on purpose.

components.label: Apical vertex model
components.plain: A two-dimensional mechanical model of a cell sheet. It passed 57 of 57 criteria under its second protocol, after the first judged run failed.

components.label: Protein-cage assembly
components.plain: Protein cages forming from folded subunits drawn from finite pools, with an experimental link to cell models. Folding itself is out of scope.

components.label: Other model modules
components.plain: Model modules not grouped elsewhere on this map.

components.label: Coherent cell model
components.plain: One cell in which many processes share the same inventories and predict several measured responses.

components.label: Integrated tissue unit
components.plain: Mechanics, transport and the cell lifecycle together on changing geometry.

components.label: First organ
components.plain: The simplest useful organ, expressed as a data definition. The organ and species are not yet chosen.

components.label: Coupled organs
components.plain: Two or more organs linked through explicit transport and signalling.

components.label: Operator contract
components.plain: What every operator must declare: the state it owns, what it writes and reads, its energy bookings and its conflicts. Checked when a model is built. A matrix of which of the composite's 19 operators can run together is regenerated from these declarations by a test (15 November 2026).

components.label: Scoped composition (door S)
components.plain: How several operators share one field. Today one operator supplies a field and replaces all of it, so two operators that touch different cells of the same field cannot be combined. In the rework each operator declares which cells or nodes it reads and changes, whether its change adds, multiplies or replaces, and at which stage of the step; the composite model then merges the changes place by place. Two operators that change separate places must give the same result in either order, and an overlap is refused unless a rule says how to combine it. Its design note was proposed on 15 November 2026. Its test case is a chain: a dose in the bath, uptake, a compartment, and a reaction inside it. Built on the integration branch by 15 November 2026, where the saved worlds give the same results bit for bit; not on main.

components.label: Compartment identity map
components.plain: A map, kept beside the arrays of numbers, that says for each compartment inside a cell its identity, its owner, its role (cytosol, lysosome, vesicle, ER or mitochondrion), where it is stored and which membrane bounds it. A first form is on main since 15 November 2026: the cell-owned compartments operator records these for each compartment it declares, as information only. The target, specified and reserved in the rework, is that laws address a species in a named compartment, so that one law serves the cytosol, a lysosome and a mitochondrion alike, and two compartments in one cell stay distinct. That part is built with its first user after the round, and is not on main.

components.label: Ownership apart from solver cost
components.plain: Three things that are tied together today are kept apart: owning a population on a membrane, changing the membrane's geometry or capacitance, and making a solver recompute, such as the refresh of the electric field. A change of occupancy then costs only what its physics requires. The site-occupancy operator already has an owner of its own for this reason, which avoids the field refresh and its limit of 64 nodes. The general rule is specified and reserved in the rework: it lands with its first user, under a narrow check of the worlds it touches. Not on main.

components.label: Endogenous lifecycle
components.plain: Division triggered by a cell's own growth or regulation, with repeated births and deaths. Its first milestone is set (D176, 15 November 2026): division timed by the cell's state, on a tree of daughters declared in advance, with fixed fractions and anchors. It is queued behind the modular rework and the priority features, unless it can proceed independently. Mitosis itself is further down the road.

components.label: Internal compartment (FR-1)
components.plain: A closed compartment inside a cell: a finite node the cell owns, bounded by one patch of its membrane, with its own volume and its own rows of the shared inventory. The user's high priority (14 November 2026). Its design is accepted (D169, 14 November 2026). components.label: Compartment pH (FR-4)
components.plain: Protons as a species, a pump that acidifies a compartment against its gradient, and buffering. Since 15 November 2026 it is one of the two priority users of the modular rework (D176), and its design note was proposed the same day: protons are one species whose free part is set by a fast buffer rule at every stage, the proton pump is a transporter law on the compartment's membrane, counterions are explicit, and its first case runs on fuel held constant. Its independent references landed on main the same day, written by a separate agent that read no engine code. In its first world the compartment acidifies from pH 7.2 to about 5.1 against its gradient, while the cytoplasm stays within 0.02 pH; without the counterion route it stalls. They also found one of the design's checks too loose, and the design now uses a check that depends on the state. Its pump and buffer are built on the integration branch, where a development run of the first world agrees with the reference to about 1e-12 pH over 900 s. Nothing is judged: its protocols are proposed, and are registered and judged after the rework lands. Not on main.

components.label: Transfer across an internal membrane (FR-5)

The other priority user of the modular rework (D176, 15 November 2026). Its design is in the note proposed with compartment pH the same day: damage is the existing injury and resealing law on the compartment's membrane, and the damage and the pH each act on the leak and on the transfer as control factors. capabilities.label: Gap junctions
capabilities.plain: Neighbouring cells exchange ions through gated junctions, and a new cell forms its junctions over time. Since 15 November 2026 the amount of a molecule can set how available a junction is, numerically qualified in its scope. Planned after the rework of the tissue model: a junction law without a gate, for excitable tissue.

capabilities.label: Space between cells
capabilities.plain: The fluid around cells holds its own ions and electric fields, with barriers between regions. Since 14 November 2026 the composition of a held bath can also change on a schedule, for a dose or a wash: implemented and guarded, admitted only for steps that were measured, and not yet qualified.

sources.where: Parity rungs P2 and P4 pass
FR-1 milestone 1, FR-10 milestone 2 and FR-3 milestone 1 landed (15 November 2026)

capabilities.label: Water and cell volume
capabilities.plain: Water follows osmotic pressure, so cells swell, shrink and regulate their volume.

sources.where: Osmotic water and volume qualified and landed

capabilities.label: Calcium and the ER
capabilities.plain: Calcium moves between the cytoplasm and the ER store, with IP3-triggered release. Tested on synthetic cases, in the earlier tissue families only. Planned: calcium handling moves into the composite model with excitable tissue (D167). A compartment that a cell owns can be declared since 15 November 2026, the first step toward the ER as a compartment for any species; no physics uses it yet.

sources.where: D167: The feature-request order and the staged move of old-family physics are adopted

capabilities.label: Fuel (ATP)
capabilities.plain: Pumps draw on a finite pool of ATP that has to be regenerated. That runs in the earlier tissue families; in the composite model fuel is held constant. Designed, not yet on main: ATP, ADP and phosphate become ordinary species of the shared inventory, made and spent by reactions and drawn on by pumps (D176, 15 November 2026). The first case is one regeneration reaction and one pump sharing a finite amount of fuel.

sources.where: D176: The modular rework proceeds, with FR-4 and FR-5 as its priority consumers

capabilities.label: Mitochondria
capabilities.plain: Mitochondria exchange ions with the cytoplasm and carry their own voltage. Respiration and ATP synthesis are not modelled. This runs in the earlier tissue families only, and moves into the composite model when a use needs it (D167). Designed, not yet on main: a compartment identity that lets one law address a species in the cytosol, a lysosome or a mitochondrion alike.

sources.where: D167: The feature-request order and the staged move of old-family physics are adopted

capabilities.label: Regulatory circuits
capabilities.plain: Small gene circuits that switch a cell between states, alone or in a two-cell model.

sources.where: What Cells can do: Regulatory cell state

capabilities.label: Gene regulation in tissue
capabilities.plain: Gene networks that set how much of each protein is made, coupled to the tissue. Planned; the full track is held (D145).

sources.where: Where things stand: New biology in the engine
Status on 14 November 2026, and the working order (D156)

capabilities.label: Golgi and trafficking
capabilities.plain: New proteins would pass from the ER through the Golgi to the membrane or out of the cell. Planned, not started. Its pool of vesicles is the kind of closed compartment that feature request FR-1 asks for, whose first milestone, the declaration of a compartment a cell owns, landed on 15 November 2026.

capabilities.label: Protein assembly
capabilities.plain: Protein cages build up from folded subunits drawn from a finite pool. Assembly is modelled as bonds forming and breaking, not as molecules moving in space. Folding is out of scope.

left_out.reason: the cage is a designed protein, not a part of a cell
left_out.why: The user, 15 November 2026: protein assemblies are one feature today and out of character with the rest of the picture, whose parts are all real or planned things of a cell; assembly may return later for a real machine, such as a proteasome. While this entry stands, the scene builder leaves the capability out of the scene, with every link to it, puts the note below on the engine parts that implement it, and uses the wordings below in place of the texts that name cages. Remove this entry and all of that comes back as it was.
left_out.engine_note: Its cage is left out of the Cell view and the Protein atlas for now: it is a designed protein, not a part of a cell.

Models that run on their own: vertex mechanics and the regulatory circuits.

capabilities.label: Molecular machines
capabilities.plain: Larger machines such as the proteasome. A goal: they will mostly be modelled in aggregate and drawn as illustrations.

capabilities.label: Cell chemistry
capabilities.plain: Chemical reactions inside compartments, with mass and energy accounted for. Reactions between species of the tissue's shared inventory are numerically qualified since 15 November 2026, within the scope of the Turing-pattern protocol MG0c and on the CPU; the earlier compartment chemistry is tested on synthetic cases. Designed, not yet on main: fuel molecules as species of that inventory, and compartments inside the cell that hold species of their own.

Status on 14 November 2026, and the working order (D156)

capabilities.label: Secreted signals
capabilities.plain: Signalling molecules spread between cells and are cleared. That transport and clearance are numerically qualified in the composite model, with a held source (D150 v1). Release, uptake and production are implemented and guarded by tests, not yet qualified; release and uptake are a driven route that books work, not passive permeation. Since 15 November 2026 binding sites that such molecules occupy and leave are implemented and guarded, as a first milestone.

sources.where: Secreted-species transport (D150 v1) is numerically qualified
FR-1 milestone 1, FR-10 milestone 2 and FR-3 milestone 1 landed (15 November 2026)

capabilities.label: Injury and repair
capabilities.plain: A membrane injury leaks ions and reseals. The resealing follows a set schedule. This runs in the earlier tissue families only; the injury law is to move into the composite model as an operator, for feature request FR-5 (D167).

sources.where: D167: The feature-request order and the staged move of old-family physics are adopted

capabilities.label: Cell division
capabilities.plain: A cell divides into two daughters on a set schedule, splitting its contents, membrane and channels with closed accounts. Division triggered by the cell itself is planned: its first milestone, timing by the cell's state on a tree of daughters declared in advance, is set (D176) and queued behind the rework of the tissue model.

sources.where: D176: The modular rework proceeds, with FR-4 and FR-5 as its priority consumers

capabilities.label: Cell replacement
capabilities.plain: Cells are removed and replaced on a schedule, and newcomers form junctions over time. This is how the heredity experiments turn a tissue over.

capabilities.label: Tissue mechanics
capabilities.plain: Cells in a sheet pull on their shared edges and relax to mechanical equilibrium. Cells cannot yet swap neighbours.

capabilities.label: Cell sheets
capabilities.plain: A sheet of 127 coupled cells runs on ordinary processors today; the judged heredity experiment E07-v1 used it, and development runs of an excitable front on it landed on 15 November 2026. The full tissue of 825 electrical nodes needs faster hardware or a long-time method.

scales.label: Molecules
scales.plain: Channels, pumps and protein cages are modelled as populations and counts, not atom by atom. Shapes drawn at this scale are illustrations.
scales.note: Assembly from prefolded proteins is mostly modelled, not simulated physically.

scales.label: One cell
scales.plain: The current focus: a coherent model of one cell, where many processes share the same inventories.
scales.note: The cell is drawn in the shape that the species shown gives it. The engine gives a cell a volume and a membrane area, not a shape. The cut removes the cell's top, which is kept as a dashed outline. Where the cell is one of a layer, its neighbours and the lined plate under the layer are scenery.

scales.label: Tissue
scales.plain: Sheets of coupled cells run today. An integrated tissue unit with mechanics and the lifecycle is a later gate.
scales.note: The sheet is a single layer of the cells of the species shown. The cells outlined beyond the sheet's edge are scenery.

scales.label: Organ
scales.plain: A first whole organ, defined as data. Planned; the organ and species are not yet chosen.
scales.note: The outline drawn is a placeholder, from the species shown. Nothing at this scale is simulated. The sizes are indicative.

scales.label: Whole organism
scales.plain: Interacting organ systems, and in time whole animals. A long-term goal; nothing is built.
scales.note: The outline drawn is a placeholder, from the species shown. Nothing at this scale is simulated. The sizes are indicative.
